div.span: - The SSH client dials the instance public DNS name on port 22 and offers the private key you downloaded when you created the key pair.

div.b: The internet gateway lets the packet into the VPC

div.span: - The subnet is public because its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to this gateway. Without that route the instance would have no way in or out.

div.b: The security group filters the traffic

div.span: - It is a stateful firewall around the instance. One inbound rule allows port 22 from your IP; every other source is dropped before it reaches the instance.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 315px; margin-left: 1213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: The instance authenticates you with the key pair

div.span: - AWS placed the public half of the key pair inside the instance when it launched. Your private key proves who you are; there is no password.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 403px; margin-left: 1213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: The EBS volume holds the operating system

div.span: - The root volume was created from the AMI and keeps your files while the instance is stopped. It is attached over the network, not built into the server.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 578px; height: 1px; padding-top: 492px; margin-left: 1230px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: What to look for in this diagram

div.span: - Nesting: the instance sits inside a subnet, the subnet inside a VPC, the VPC inside one Region of your account. Every box is a choice you made in the wizard.
- Two different controls: the security group decides which packets arrive; the key pair decides who may log in. Opening port 22 still needs a key.
- The public address is not permanent: stopping and starting the instance hands it a new one, which is why you look it up again after a restart.
- Storage is separate: the volume survives a stop, so the instance keeps its files; terminating the instance deletes it.
